title: The wise minister
hookLine: Vidhura is won at dice by a spirit and teaches him on the way (Jataka 545)

cards: A stranger arrives at the king's court with a jewel and a horse that can run through the sky, and offers a game of dice. If he loses, the king takes both.
If he wins, he wants one thing: the king's minister, Vidhura, known across the kingdom for his wisdom. The king rolls, and loses. The stranger is a yakkha, a fierce spirit, named Punnaka.

teach.h: A QUEEN LONGS FOR HIS HEART.
teach.b: Far below, in the realm of the nagas, a queen named Vimala has heard Vidhura speak about goodness, and she longs for his heart. Her daughter, Irandati, offers to marry whoever brings it, and Punnaka sets out to get it.
But he takes the word literally.
On the journey, with Vidhura clinging to the horse's tail through the sky, he tries to frighten the minister to death, and finally tries to dash him from a mountaintop.
Vidhura stays unshaken, and asks a calm question: why are you doing this? Punnaka tells him.
Instead of pleading for his life, Vidhura teaches him how a good person lives, keeps faith with friends, and repays kindness. Punnaka is changed, and offers to take him home.
Vidhura says no; take me to the nagas, as you promised. In the naga palace it comes out at last. The queen never wanted flesh.
The heart she longed for was his wisdom, and Vidhura gives it, teaching the naga king and queen, and then goes home. Tradition pairs this tale with truth, sacca. Notice where the teaching happens.
Not in a temple, not at court. In the hands of someone trying to kill him, on a mountaintop, on the worst day of his life. Vidhura treats even that as a place to teach.

how: Vidhura's story is told as an example of the perfection of truth; in Buddhist practice, sharing the teaching is valued as a gift in itself, the gift of the Dhamma.

o: a spirit who wins at dice
a wise one, a learned person

games.q: who did what in Vidhura's story: tap the pairs.
p: the yakkha who won Vidhura at dice
the naga queen who longed for his heart
taught the spirit who tried to kill him
lost his minister in a game

s: the naga queen wanted Vidhura's heart cut out
the heart she longed for was his wisdom; only Punnaka took it literally.
Vidhura pleaded for his life on the mountain
he asked why, calmly, and then taught Punnaka how a good person lives.
the king lost Vidhura in a game of dice
Punnaka staked a jewel and a sky-horse against the minister, and won.

games.q: you're Vidhura. you've taught Punnaka, and now he offers to take you home instead. what do you do?
o: go on to the naga realm, as he promised.
send him to the nagas alone with a message.
games.why: he insists on going to the nagas, where the queen's wish turns out to be for his wisdom, and he teaches there before going home.

practice: Think of somewhere today will put you that you didn't choose: a meeting, a waiting room, a hard conversation.

Picture yourself there and ask what you could offer, not a lecture, but patience, a steady voice, a question asked kindly, and rest with the picture of being useful exactly where you didn't want to be.

wordCard.voice: Pandita. A wise one: what Vidhura was called, won at dice and carried off by a spirit who meant to kill him, and taught his captor instead. Today's word.

orig.note: Pali pandita, a wise one; Vidhura is called Vidhurapandita.

carryVoice: Your line: he taught his captor. The heart they wanted was his wisdom all along. Day eight hundred forty-five, done.
